query: what safety level are the steering feel components developed to?
note: THE acceptance case for the whole index, and it is the one documents-selftest already guards as a predicate. `walk-cost` step 3 reads this classification out of a file it opens by a path typed into its own source, and the walk's output claims 'this cost item only exists if somebody read the document.' Nobody read anything. If asking in English does not surface §3, the index is decoration and the hardcoded path cannot be removed. Scored at the SECTION, not the file: §1 (scope), §2 (hazard) and §4 (limitations) are all in the same document and none of them states the classification.

query: is the damping safety decomposition valid for a new programme or does it have to be redone?
note: The most expensive sentence in the estate. §4 says the decomposition is PLATFORM SPECIFIC and that a programme allocating a higher ASIL directly to the damping function invalidates it. That is the difference between 'carryover, no cost' and a re-assessment, and it sits one section below the classification everybody retrieves instead. A retriever that returns §3 here has found the right document and the wrong answer.

The case only the KEYWORD arm can win. Embeddings treat SR-EPS-0421 and SR-EPS-0407 as near-identical strings — a rare identifier has no neighbours in embedding space — and the K2 spec contains both. If the full-text half of hybrid search stops running, this is the case that goes red first, which is why the runner refuses to record a measurement when the keyword arm did not run.

query: how much force must the EPS assembly deliver at the rack including internal losses?
note: The mirror of ret-003: the question shares almost no vocabulary with the requirement id that answers it, so this is the case the DENSE arm has to win. Twelve programmes in this corpus state a rack force with different numbers, so the label carries the path and the requirement id — retrieving PRG-TDR-01's rack force here is a wrong answer that looks exactly like a right one.

query: does the damping software already meet the safety level the K2 programme requires?
note: THE HARD CASE, and the one a reranker has the most room to move. Answering it needs TWO passages from two different repositories: K2 requires the damping function at ASIL D, and the 2021 assessment classified SWC-DAMP at ASIL B. Neither passage alone says anything is wrong — the finding only exists in the pair, so a retriever that returns one of the two scores 0.5 and fails, correctly. Deliberately NOT expecting the MISRA report or the header, which state ASIL B a third and fourth time: this asks for the requirement and the governing assessment, not for every mention.

query: why was a MISRA rule deviated for the damping module?
note: A `.txt` static-analysis report with NO heading structure at all — the chunker has nothing to build a trail from, so this passage is labelled by its path alone. Deviation D-07 is the only explanation of the three-way ASIL disagreement anywhere in 1,069 files. There are 73 near-identical MISRA reports in the index and they differ mostly by module name, which makes this a genuine discrimination test rather than a lookup.

query: was any effort booked to a charge code that also covers unrelated work?
note: THE CASE THAT JUSTIFIES THE LABEL SCHEME, and — unexpectedly — the case that exposed an RRF defect. Closure reports are what `find_comparable_work` prices from, there are 220 of them, they are structurally near-identical, and NOT ONE has a heading trail: a trail-only label would make this whole document class unnameable and drop it out of every measurement without a word. EFF-2021-0443 is the one that booked a production-line transfer to a gearbox housing charge code 'for want of a separate code', so its reported hours are contaminated and a median over it is wrong. MEASURED 2026-09-14: the KEYWORD arm ranks this document FIRST for this query — the shared terms are real ('booked', 'code', 'work') — and the dense arm does not return it in the top 200 at all. Reciprocal rank fusion then buries it at position 35, because RRF rewards agreement between arms and a single-arm hit scores 1/61 while any document BOTH arms rank 50th scores 2/110, which is larger. So this case does not show the retriever cannot find the document; it shows the FUSER discards what only one arm found.

query: where is the actual behaviour of the hysteresis compensation module recorded?
note: Covers the CODE CHUNKER, which produced 1,027 of the 3,854 indexed passages and until now had no retrieval measurement of any kind — only `code-chunk:check`, which asserts the chunker splits correctly and says nothing about whether the results can be found. The answer is the test file's banner, which states plainly that the 2015 design note has gone stale and the tests are the surviving specification. Labelled at the file because a banner carries no symbol; the function passages in the same file label as `§test_Hyst_Apply_rejects_null()` and would not satisfy this. THIS IS THE CASE THE RERANKER MAKES WORSE, and it is the strongest argument for leaving it off: the cross-encoder promotes `module-hysteresis_comp.md` — the STALE design note this case exists to rank below the tests — above the test file. Relevance and currency are different questions and a relevance model cannot see the second one.
